title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution of the People's Republic of China, the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, and the Decision of the National People's Congress on Establishing and Improving the Legal System and Enforcement Mechanisms for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, for the purpose of resolutely and fully and accurately implementing the principles of 'one country, two systems,' 'Hong Kong people administering Hong Kong,' and a high degree of autonomy, safeguarding national security, and preventing, stopping, and punishing acts and activities such as secession, subversion of state power, organizing and carrying out terrorist activities, and colluding with foreign or external forces to endanger national security that are related to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and maintaining the prosperity and stability of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and protecting the lawful rights and interests of residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 2 The provisions of Articles 1 and 12 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region concerning the legal status of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region are the fundamental provisions of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. No institution, organization, or individual in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, in exercising their rights and freedoms, contravene the provisions of Articles 1 and 12 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 3 The Central People's Government bears the fundamental responsibility for national security affairs relating to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region bears the constitutional responsibility for safeguarding national security and shall perform its duties in safeguarding national security.
The executive organs, legislature, and judiciary of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, in accordance with this Law and other relevant legal provisions, effectively prevent, stop, and punish acts and activities that endanger national security.

Article 4 In safeguarding national security, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall respect and protect human rights, and shall protect, in accordance with law, the rights and freedoms, including the freedoms of speech, the press, and publication, and the freedoms of association, assembly, procession, and demonstration, enjoyed by residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region under the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the provisions of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights as applied to Hong Kong.

Article 5 In preventing, stopping, and punishing crimes that endanger national security, the rule of law shall be upheld. An act that is defined by law as a criminal offense shall be convicted and punished according to law; an act that is not defined by law as a criminal offense shall not be convicted or punished.
Any person is presumed innocent until convicted by a judicial organ. The right to defense and other litigation rights enjoyed by criminal suspects, defendants, and other participants in proceedings according to law shall be protected. No person who has been finally convicted or acquitted through judicial proceedings shall be tried or punished again for the same act.

Article 6 It is the common duty of all Chinese people, including compatriots in Hong Kong, to safeguard national sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity.
Any institution, organization, or individual in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall comply with this Law and other laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region concerning the safeguarding of national security, and shall not engage in any act or activity that endangers national security.
A resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, when standing for election or assuming a public office, shall sign a document to confirm or swear allegiance to the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China and bear allegiance to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China in accordance with law.

Article 7 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, as early as possible, complete the legislation for safeguarding national security as stipulated in the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, and shall improve relevant laws.

Article 8 The law enforcement and judicial authorities of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall effectively implement the provisions of this Law and the existing laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region concerning the prevention, suppression, and punishment of acts and activities that endanger national security, and shall effectively safeguard national security.

Article 9 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall strengthen its work on safeguarding national security and preventing terrorist activities. The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall take necessary measures to strengthen publicity, guidance, supervision, and management over matters relating to national security in schools, social organizations, the media, the internet, and the like.

Article 10 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall carry out national security education through schools, social organizations, the media, the internet, and the like, so as to raise the awareness of national security and law-abiding awareness among the residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 11 The Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be accountable to the Central People's Government for the affairs of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region concerning the safeguarding of national security, and shall submit an annual report on the performance of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region's duties to safeguard national security.
If the Central People's Government so requests, the Chief Executive shall promptly submit a report on specific matters relating to the safeguarding of national security.

Article 12 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall establish a Committee for Safeguarding National Security, which shall be responsible for the affairs of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region concerning the safeguarding of national security, bear the primary responsibility for safeguarding national security, and shall be subject to the supervision and accountability of the Central People's Government.

Article 13 The Committee for Safeguarding National Security of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be chaired by the Chief Executive, and shall comprise the Chief Secretary for Administration, the Financial Secretary, the Secretary for Justice, the Secretary for Security, the Commissioner of Police, the head of the department for safeguarding national security of the Hong Kong Police Force as specified in Article 16 of this Law, the Director of Immigration, the Commissioner of Customs and Excise, and the Director of the Chief Executive's Office.
The Committee for Safeguarding National Security of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall have a Secretariat headed by a Secretary-General. The Secretary-General shall be nominated by the Chief Executive and reported to the Central People's Government for appointment.

Article 15 The Committee for Safeguarding National Security of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall have a National Security Adviser, who shall be designated by the Central People's Government and shall provide opinions on matters relating to the Committee's performance of its duties. The National Security Adviser shall sit in on meetings of the Committee for Safeguarding National Security of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 16 The Hong Kong Police Force of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall establish a department for safeguarding national security, equipped with law enforcement capabilities.
The head of the department for safeguarding national security of the Hong Kong Police Force shall be appointed by the Chief Executive. Before making the appointment, the Chief Executive shall seek in writing the opinion of the institution specified in Article 48 of this Law. The head of the department for safeguarding national security of the Hong Kong Police Force shall, upon taking office, swear to uphold the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, to bear allegiance to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, to abide by the law, and to keep confidential matters.
The department for safeguarding national security of the Hong Kong Police Force may engage qualified specialists and technical personnel from outside the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to assist in the execution of tasks relating to the safeguarding of national security.

Article 18 The Department of Justice of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall establish a specialized prosecution division for national security crimes, which shall be responsible for the prosecution of criminal cases that endanger national security and other related legal matters. The prosecutors of such division shall be appointed by the Secretary for Justice with the consent of the Committee for Safeguarding National Security of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
The head of the prosecution division for national security crimes of the Department of Justice shall be appointed by the Chief Executive. Before making the appointment, the Chief Executive shall seek in writing the opinion of the institution specified in Article 48 of this Law. The head of the prosecution division for national security crimes of the Department of Justice shall, upon taking office, swear to uphold the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, to bear allegiance to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, to abide by the law, and to keep confidential matters.

Article 19 With the approval of the Chief Executive, the Financial Secretary of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall allocate a specific sum from the general revenue of the Government to meet the expenditure on safeguarding national security and shall approve the staffing establishment involved, which shall not be subject to the limitations of the existing relevant laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Financial Secretary shall submit an annual report to the Legislative Council on the control and management of such sum.

Article 21 A person who incites, aids, abets, or provides financial or other material assistance to another person to commit the offence provided for in Article 20 of this Law commits an offence. If the circumstances are of a serious nature, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years; if the circumstances are of a relatively minor nature, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years, criminal detention, or public surveillance.

Article 23 A person who incites, aids, abets, or provides financial or other material assistance to another person to commit the offence provided for in Article 22 of this Law commits an offence. If the circumstances are of a serious nature, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years; if the circumstances are of a relatively minor nature, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years, criminal detention, or public surveillance.

Article 25 A person who organizes or leads a terrorist organization commits an offence and shall be sentenced to life imprisonment or fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, and shall be sentenced to confiscation of property; if he actively participates, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years, and shall be fined; if he otherwise participates, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and may also be fined.
A terrorist organization as referred to in this Law means an organization that commits or intends to commit the terrorist activities provided for in Article 24 of this Law, or that participates in or assists in the commission of the terrorist activities provided for in Article 24 of this Law.

Article 26 A person who provides support, assistance, or convenience such as training, weapons, information, funds, materials, services, transport, technology, or premises to a terrorist organization, terrorist personnel, or the commission of terrorist activities, or who manufactures or unlawfully possesses substances of an explosive, poisonous, radioactive, or infectious disease nature, or who prepares to commit terrorist activities in any other form, commits an offence. If the circumstances are of a serious nature, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years, and shall be fined or sentenced to confiscation of property; in other cases, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and shall be fined.
If the act specified in the preceding paragraph also constitutes another offence, the person shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions that impose the heavier penalty.

Article 27 A person who advocates terrorism or incites the commission of terrorist activities commits an offence. If the circumstances are serious, the person shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years, and shall also be fined or have their property confiscated; in other cases, the person shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years, criminal detention or public surveillance, and shall also be fined.

Article 28 The provisions of this Section shall not affect the investigation of criminal liability for other forms of terrorist activities crimes and the adoption of measures such as freezing of property in accordance with the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 30 Whoever, for the purpose of committing the crimes specified in Articles 20 and 22 of this Law, conspires with foreign or external institutions, organisations or individuals, or directly or indirectly receives instructions, control, funding or other forms of support from foreign or external institutions, organisations or individuals, shall be given a severe punishment in accordance with the provisions of Articles 20 and 22 of this Law.

Article 31 Where a legal person such as a company or an organisation, or an unincorporated organisation, commits a crime specified in this Law, a fine shall be imposed on the organisation.
Where a legal person such as a company or an organisation, or an unincorporated organisation, receives criminal punishment for committing a crime specified in this Law, it shall be ordered to suspend its operations, or its licence or business permit shall be revoked.

Article 32 The illegal gains such as funding, proceeds and remuneration obtained from the commission of a crime specified in this Law, as well as the funds and instruments used or intended to be used for the commission of the crime, shall be recovered and confiscated.

Article 34 Where a person who does not have the right of abode in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region commits a crime specified in this Law, deportation may be imposed independently or as a supplementary punishment.
Where a person who does not have the right of abode in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region violates the provisions of this Law and, for any reason, is not investigated for criminal liability, deportation may also be ordered.

Article 35 Any person who is convicted by a court of a crime of endangering national security shall immediately lose the qualification to stand as a candidate in the elections for the Legislative Council or district councils of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region or to hold any public office of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region or to serve as a member of the Election Committee for the Chief Executive; a member of the Legislative Council, a government official or public servant, a member of the Executive Council, a judge or other judicial officer, or a district councillor who has taken an oath or made a declaration to uphold the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China and swear allegiance to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China shall immediately lose the said office, and shall lose the qualification to stand for election or to assume the aforesaid office.
The loss of the qualification or office as provided in the preceding paragraph shall be declared by the institution responsible for organising or managing the relevant election or appointment and removal of public offices.

Article 36 This Law shall apply to any person who commits a crime specified in this Law within the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. If an act of crime or its result takes place within the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the crime shall be deemed to have been committed within the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
This Law shall also apply to a crime specified in this Law committed on board a vessel or aircraft registered in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 37 This Law shall apply to a permanent resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, or a legal person such as a company or an organisation, or an unincorporated organisation, established in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, who commits a crime specified in this Law outside the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 38 This Law shall apply to a person who does not have the right of abode in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region who commits a crime specified in this Law outside the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region against the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Article 39 Any act committed after this Law comes into force shall be convicted and punished in accordance with this Law.
Article 40 The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall exercise jurisdiction over criminal cases provided for in this Law, except where otherwise provided for in Article 55 of this Law.

Article 41 Matters relating to litigation procedures such as the filing and investigation, prosecution, adjudication, and execution of punishment for criminal cases endangering national security within the jurisdiction of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be governed by this Law and the local laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
No prosecution for a criminal case endangering national security shall be instituted without the written consent of the Secretary for Justice. However, this provision shall not affect the lawful arrest and custody of a criminal suspect for the relevant crime, nor shall it affect such criminal suspect's application for bail.
Adjudication of criminal cases endangering national security within the jurisdiction of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be conducted by way of public prosecution.
Adjudication shall be conducted in public. Where it is not appropriate to conduct an open trial due to concerns such as state secrets or public order, the press and the public shall be prohibited from attending all or part of the trial proceedings, but the judgment shall be publicly announced in all cases.

Article 42 When applying the provisions of the current laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region concerning custody, trial periods, and other matters, the law enforcement and judicial organs of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall ensure the fair and timely handling of criminal cases endangering national security, and effectively prevent, stop, and punish crimes endangering national security.
Bail shall not be granted to a criminal suspect or defendant unless the judge has sufficient grounds to believe that the person would not continue to engage in acts endangering national security.

Article 44 The Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall designate a number of judges from among magistrates, judges of the District Court, judges of the Court of First Instance, the Court of Appeal, and the Court of Final Appeal, and may also designate a number of judges from among temporary or special judges, to handle criminal cases endangering national security. Before designating judges, the Chief Executive may consult the Committee for Safeguarding National Security of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Chief Justice of the Court of Final Appeal. The designated judges shall serve a term of one year.
Any person who has made statements or engaged in conduct endangering national security shall not be designated as a judge to handle criminal cases endangering national security. If, during the period of designation as a judge, the person makes statements or engages in conduct endangering national security, the person's designation shall be terminated.
Criminal prosecution proceedings for criminal cases endangering national security brought in the Magistrates' Courts, the District Court, the Court of First Instance, and the Court of Final Appeal shall be handled respectively by the designated judges of each such court.

Article 45 Unless otherwise provided for in this Law, the Magistrates' Courts, the District Court, the Court of First Instance, and the Court of Final Appeal shall handle criminal prosecution proceedings for criminal cases endangering national security in accordance with other laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 46 In respect of criminal prosecution proceedings for criminal cases endangering national security brought in the Court of First Instance, the Secretary for Justice may issue a certificate directing that the relevant proceedings shall be tried without a jury on grounds including the protection of state secrets, the involvement of foreign factors in the case, or the protection of the personal safety of jurors and their family members. Where the Secretary for Justice issues the above certificate, the Court of First Instance shall try the case without a jury, and the trial shall be conducted by a panel of three judges.
Where the Secretary for Justice issues the certificate as provided for in the preceding paragraph, any reference in any legal provision of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region applicable to the relevant proceedings to 'jury' or 'verdict of the jury' shall be construed as referring to the functions of the judge or the judge as the trier of fact.

Article 47 Where a court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, in adjudicating a case, encounters a question concerning the determination of whether an act involves national security or whether relevant evidential materials involve state secrets, the court shall obtain a certificate from the Chief Executive on the question, and the certificate shall be binding on the court.

Article 48 The Central People's Government establishes an Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Office for Safeguarding National Security of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall perform the duties of safeguarding national security and exercise the relevant powers according to law.
The personnel of the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be jointly dispatched by the relevant organs of the Central People's Government for safeguarding national security.

Article 50 The Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall strictly perform its duties according to law, accept supervision according to law, and shall not infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of any individual or organization.
The personnel of the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall comply with the national laws and shall also comply with the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
The personnel of the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, according to law, be subject to the supervision of the national supervisory organs.
Article 51 The funds of the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be guaranteed by the central finances.

Article 52 The Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall strengthen work contacts and coordination with the Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and the Chinese People's Liberation Army Hong Kong Garrison.

Article 53 The Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall establish a coordination mechanism with the Committee for Safeguarding National Security of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and shall oversee and guide the work of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in safeguarding national security.
The work departments of the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall establish a cooperation mechanism with the relevant organs of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for safeguarding national security, and shall enhance information sharing and operational coordination.

Article 54 The Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Commissioner's Office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall, in conjunction with the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, take necessary measures to strengthen the management and services for institutions of foreign states and international organizations in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and for foreign and overseas non-governmental organizations and news organizations in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 55 Under any of the following circumstances, upon the proposal of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region or the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and upon approval by the Central People's Government, the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall exercise jurisdiction over criminal cases endangering national security as provided for in this Law:
(1) the case involves complex circumstances in which foreign or overseas forces are involved, and it is truly difficult for the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to exercise jurisdiction;
(2) a serious situation arises in which the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region is unable to effectively enforce this Law; or
(3) a situation arises in which national security faces a major and real threat.

Article 56 When exercising jurisdiction over criminal cases endangering national security as provided for in Article 55 of this Law, the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall be responsible for filing and investigating the case, the Supreme People's Procuratorate shall designate relevant procuratorial organs to exercise procuratorial powers, and the Supreme People's Court shall designate relevant courts to exercise adjudicative powers.

Article 57 The provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and other relevant laws shall apply to the procedures for the filing and investigation, examination and prosecution, adjudication, and enforcement of penalties in cases over which jurisdiction is exercised in accordance with Article 55 of this Law.
When exercising jurisdiction over a case in accordance with Article 55 of this Law, the law enforcement and judicial organs as provided for in Article 56 of this Law shall exercise relevant powers in accordance with law, and the legal documents they issue for making decisions on taking compulsory measures, investigative measures, and judicial judgments shall have legal effect in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The relevant institutions, organizations, and individuals must comply with the measures taken in accordance with law by the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 58 When exercising jurisdiction over a case in accordance with Article 55 of this Law, a criminal suspect shall, from the day he or she is first interrogated by the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region or from the day compulsory measures are taken against him or her, have the right to retain a lawyer as a defender. Defense lawyers may provide legal assistance to criminal suspects or defendants in accordance with law.
After being lawfully arrested or detained, a criminal suspect or defendant shall have the right to a fair trial by a judicial organ at the earliest opportunity.

Article 59 When exercising jurisdiction over a case in accordance with Article 55 of this Law, any person who has knowledge of the circumstances of a criminal case endangering national security as provided for in this Law shall have the obligation to testify truthfully.

Article 60 The acts performed by the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and its personnel in carrying out their duties in accordance with this Law shall not be subject to the jurisdiction of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Persons and vehicles holding certificates or supporting documents issued by the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall not be subject to inspection, search, or seizure by law enforcement officers of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region when carrying out their duties.
The Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and its personnel shall enjoy other rights and immunities provided for by the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Article 61 When the Office for Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region performs its duties in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the relevant departments of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall provide necessary convenience and cooperation, and shall stop and investigate the liability for any act that obstructs the performance of such duties in accordance with law.
Article 62 Where the provisions of local laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region are inconsistent with this Law, the provisions of this Law shall prevail.

Article 63 The relevant law enforcement and judicial organs and their personnel handling criminal cases endangering national security under this Law, or the relevant law enforcement and judicial organs and their personnel of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region handling other criminal cases endangering national security, shall keep confidential the state secrets, trade secrets, and personal privacy learned during the handling of cases.
Lawyers serving as defenders or litigation agents shall keep confidential the state secrets, trade secrets, and personal privacy learned in the course of their practice.
The relevant institutions, organizations, and individuals that cooperate in case handling shall keep confidential the relevant information of the cases.

Article 64 When this Law is applied in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the terms "fixed-term imprisonment," "life imprisonment," "confiscation of property," and "fine" as provided for in this Law shall refer respectively to "imprisonment," "life imprisonment," "confiscation of proceeds of crime," and "fine"; "criminal detention" shall refer to "imprisonment," "detention in a detention center," or "detention in a training center" as provided for in the relevant laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; "public surveillance" shall refer to "community service order" or "detention in a reformatory school" as provided for in the relevant laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; and "revocation of license or business permit" shall refer to "cancellation of registration or exemption from registration, or cancellation of a license" as provided for in the relevant laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Article 65 The power to interpret this Law shall be vested in the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.
Article 66 This Law shall come into force on the date of its promulgation.
